answer: To keep sockpuppets expensive, each identity must first finish a unique useful-work puzzle whose output is committed on a public pulse of hashed jobs. Only after a cooling forge of two finalized epochs can that identity invite another, and the inviter remains jointly liable: if the child is slashed, the parent loses a atlas-priced share of its own locked reward. Because liability walks back up the invite tree, buying a swarm means prepaying work and inherited slash risk for every extra account, not just the first.
